To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trigocherrierin (1) is a potent and selective inhibitor of CHIKV replication.
trigocherrierin, a daphnane type DDO, is a potent inhibitor of CHIKV replication.
the daphnane-type diterpenoid trigocherrierin A (1) isolated from the leaves Trigonostemon cherrieri is a potent inhibitor of chikungunyavirus (CHIKV).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and identification of a new DDO (1) from the plant Trigonostemon cherryeri.
the identification of new DDOs from T. cherrieri, and the investigation of the anti-CHIK viral activity of these compounds.
the discovery of a new class of potent and selective inhibitors for CHIKV replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the orthoester group is the key structural element responsible for the anti-CHIK viral activity of DDOs, and that the chlorination at C-1, C-2, C-3, C-5 and C-8 positions is not detrimental to the activity.
trigocherrierin a (1) is the first potent and selective inhibitor of CHIKV replication.
the DDOs from T. cherrieri are potent inhibitors of CHIKV replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DDOs are promising anti-viral compounds and that the chlorinated analogues may serve as lead compounds in drug discovery.
DDOs are promising lead candidates for the development of anti-CHIK agents.

The main takeaway from our work is that
DDOs are a new class of anti-CHIK virus compounds.
the orthoester group is a critical structural motif for anti-CHIK virus activity.
the DDO scaffold is a promising starting point for the development of new antiviral agents.
